hero_copy.label: Hero introduction
hero_copy.value: I'm Haley, an instructional designer who works across learning design, sales enablement, learning technology, AI training and evaluation, and digital development.

featured_heading.label: Featured work heading
featured_heading.value: Explore the different sides of my work.

featured_intro.label: Featured work introduction
featured_intro.value: My portfolio is organized around three connected areas: instructional design, AI training and evaluation, and the workflows that help learning work move efficiently from idea to implementation and continuous improvement.

hero_title.label: About hero title
hero_title.value: Learning designed for clarity, usefulness, and performance.

hero_intro_primary.label: Primary introduction
hero_intro_primary.value: I've worked in various fields creating instructional design content. From public to private sectors, adults to children, humans to bots, I can design for all. My most recent work has focused around building content for enterprise learning environments for audiences such as sales and partner enablement, product launch support, and customer support. My projects range from interactive learning and certification pathways to LMS processes, analytics, workflow automation and project management, and custom digital content.

hero_intro_secondary.label: Background paragraph
hero_intro_secondary.value: Before moving into corporate L&D, I taught high school history and english. That classroom background, along with my Master of Education, still shapes how I think about clarity, practice, feedback, assessment, and whether learning actually supports performance.

approach_intro.label: L&D approach introduction
approach_intro.value: The format of a learning solution may change, but these are the ideas I keep coming back to when I'm deciding what to build, how it should work, and how I'll know whether it's useful.

thread_intro.label: Common thread introduction
thread_intro.value: The deliverable may change, but I tend to approach the work through the same lens. Select an area to see what that looks like in practice.

hero_intro.label: Projects hero introduction
hero_intro.value: My portfolio is organized around three areas: instructional design, AI, and workflows. Together they show both what I build and the systems, processes, and decisions behind the work.

family_intro.label: Project types introduction
family_intro.value: Choose a category to explore project examples, interactive demos, complete learning structures, AI evaluation work, and the workflows that support learning development.

hero_intro.label: Hero introduction
hero_intro.value: My instructional design work spans the full learning lifecycle—from identifying what people need to do through designing, developing, delivering, assessing, and improving the learning experience.

overview_heading.label: Overview heading
overview_heading.value: From the learning need to the learning ecosystem.

overview_body_one.label: Overview paragraph 1
overview_body_one.value: I don't think of instructional design as simply creating courses. The work starts with understanding the learner, the performance need, and the business problem before deciding what kind of learning solution actually makes sense.

overview_body_two.label: Overview paragraph 2
overview_body_two.value: Depending on the need, that solution might be a focused interaction, multimedia training asset, assessment experience, certification pathway, or a larger learning ecosystem connecting content, LMS delivery, tracking, and reporting.

examples_intro.label: Examples introduction
examples_intro.value: These examples range from individual learning interactions to complete structures for delivering, assessing, and measuring learning.

hero_intro_primary.label: Hero introduction
hero_intro_primary.value: My AI work focuses on evaluating whether generated content actually satisfies the task it was created to perform. That means looking beyond fluency and surface polish to examine accuracy, grounding, instruction adherence, completeness, consistency, usability, and overall task success.

hero_intro_secondary.label: Hero supporting paragraph
hero_intro_secondary.value: I use structured criteria, analytical review, evidence-based issue detection, actionable feedback, and quality assurance to help improve model outputs and the data used to train and evaluate AI systems.

overview_heading.label: Overview heading
overview_heading.value: Good AI evaluation starts with the task.

overview_body_one.label: Overview paragraph 1
overview_body_one.value: A response can be clear, professional, and convincing while still being wrong, incomplete, unsupported, or misaligned with what the user actually requested.

overview_body_two.label: Overview paragraph 2
overview_body_two.value: I start by understanding the task, the intended audience, the available source material or ground truth, and the criteria that define successful performance. Only then do I evaluate the output.

overview_body_three.label: Overview paragraph 3
overview_body_three.value: I also try to separate material quality issues from stylistic preference. The question isn't whether I personally would have written something differently. The question is whether the output satisfies the requirements and whether any problems meaningfully reduce its accuracy, usefulness, or reliability.

hero_intro.label: Hero introduction
hero_intro.value: I don't just think about the final learning asset. I'm also interested in the systems behind the work: how projects move from need to design, how development becomes repeatable, where AI and automation can help, and how data feeds back into better decisions.

overview_heading.label: Overview heading
overview_heading.value: Good processes make good work easier to repeat.

overview_body_one.label: Overview paragraph 1
overview_body_one.value: A strong workflow reduces unnecessary friction, creates clearer handoffs, makes quality easier to maintain, and helps teams reuse what already works.

overview_body_two.label: Overview paragraph 2
overview_body_two.value: In L&D, that can mean anything from documenting a design process to automating repetitive reporting, creating reusable development components, or using AI within a structured review loop.

overview_body_three.label: Overview paragraph 3
overview_body_three.value: I think of workflows as part of the learning solution itself because the way the work is designed, developed, deployed, tracked, and improved directly affects the final learner experience.

areas_heading.value: Explore how the work gets done.
